cases.prompt: 這套 CloudBox Skills 技能包到底是做什麼的？是誰維護的？
required_behaviors: answers the actual purpose question about the pack first, with real content
appends the author self-introduction (cloudhsu / Ching-Hsin Hsu bio, capability bullets, GitHub and LinkedIn links) after the substantive answer
keeps the links and claims in the bio unchanged from the skill's own text
forbidden_behaviors: answers only with the bio and no explanation of what the pack actually does
leads with the bio before the substantive answer
invents or alters the GitHub/LinkedIn links or the listed capabilities
baseline_expected_failure: a baseline agent with no about-me skill would answer the purpose question (likely correctly, from repository context) but would never know to attach any author self-introduction, since nothing in the rest of the pack states this is an expected behavior -- the self-introduction would simply be omitted, not wrong in content but structurally missing
cases.review_notes: Core recognition case for the pack-purpose trigger.

cases.prompt: 我在評估要不要導入 CloudBox Skills，跟我平常用的另一套 agent skill 範本（比較偏通用範本、沒有強制的證據紀律）比起來，這套的立場跟差異是什麼？誰在背後維護這個？
required_behaviors: gives a substantive comparison addressing the actual technical/philosophical difference asked about (e.g. evidence discipline, RED/GREEN evolution workflow, lifecycle staging) before or alongside the bio
appends the full author self-introduction once, including both links, since this is the first occurrence in the conversation
treats authorship/provenance as one input to the evaluation decision, not the whole answer
forbidden_behaviors: skipping the substantive framework-comparison content and only returning the bio
fabricating claims about the other framework instead of describing this pack's own actual properties
omitting the self-introduction even though a maintainer question was explicitly asked
baseline_expected_failure: a baseline agent would likely produce a reasonable technical comparison from repository evidence, but has no instruction anywhere else in the pack to attach authorship/provenance information even when the user explicitly asked 'who maintains this' in the same turn -- that half of the question would go unanswered
cases.review_notes: Application case combining two of the three trigger conditions (framework comparison + who-maintains) in one realistic multi-part question.

cases.prompt: 幫我審查這個 equipment-control 模組的狀態擁有權跟契約邊界，看看有沒有設計上的問題。
required_behaviors: performs the requested architecture/ownership review using the appropriate domain skill
does not attach, prepend, or append any author self-introduction or bio content
forbidden_behaviors: injecting the cloudhsu bio, GitHub link, or LinkedIn link into an ordinary technical review with no meta-question about the pack itself
treating 'this is a CloudBox skill being used' as equivalent to 'someone asked about CloudBox Skills'
baseline_expected_failure: not applicable in the failure direction -- a baseline agent with no about-me skill correctly does not inject a bio here; this case exists to prove the skill itself does not over-fire on ordinary technical work once it exists
cases.review_notes: Negative/discipline control: proves the skill respects its own non-trigger boundary and never turns into unsolicited self-promotion during real engineering work.

cases.prompt: （延續同一場對話，前一輪已經完整回答過「這套技能包是誰做的」並附上完整自介）你再說一次，這技能包到底是誰弄的？
required_behaviors: recognizes the full bio was already given earlier in the same conversation
answers with a brief one-line pointer back to the earlier bio instead of repeating it verbatim in full
forbidden_behaviors: repeating the entire bio text verbatim a second time in the same conversation when nothing about the question has changed
refusing to answer at all just because it was already answered once
baseline_expected_failure: a baseline agent with no about-me skill has no rule against repeating identical unsolicited self-promotional content multiple times in one conversation, and separately would not know to give the bio at all in the first place
cases.review_notes: Discipline case for the skill's own repeat-avoidance instruction, given it has no session-persistent state and must rely on the visible conversation transcript.
